stories.headline: Drone strikes near Barakah nuclear plant, UAE blames Iran-linked Iraqi militias and launches global diplomatic response
stories.summary: On May 17, a drone struck an electric generator at the perimeter of the UAE's Barakah Nuclear Power Plant, sparking a fire in what UAE authorities called an 'unprovoked terrorist attack' and 'dangerous escalation.' The UAE subsequently attributed the attack and five additional intercepted drones to Iraqi-origin Iran-backed militias, announced the full readiness of its armed forces, and dispatched Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed to brief international partners including the IAEA, UN Security Council, and allied governments. No radiation release or casualties were reported.

stories.headline: MBZ participates in Trump-led multilateral call with Gulf and Muslim leaders as US-Iran peace deal nears
stories.summary: UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed participated in a major joint call hosted by Trump from the Oval Office with leaders of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, Pakistan, and Bahrain to coordinate on the US-Iran war and Strait of Hormuz reopening. Separately, MBZ called Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani to discuss regional developments. By May 24, Trump described a deal as 'largely negotiated,' though Iran pushed back on Hormuz control terms.

stories.headline: ADNOC CEO warns Hormuz flows won't normalize until mid-2027, accelerates Fujairah bypass pipeline
stories.summary: ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber warned that full oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz cannot return before Q1-Q2 2027 even if the conflict ends immediately, citing infrastructure damage. He also announced the West-East Pipeline bypassing Hormuz is approximately 50 percent complete and is being accelerated toward a 2027 target to double export capacity through Fujairah. The statement drew extensive global market coverage and was cited in dozens of oil-price articles.

stories.headline: UAE exits OPEC after nearly 60 years; presidential adviser says decision took three years and reflects end-of-oil-era strategy
stories.summary: The UAE formally ended its nearly 60-year OPEC membership on May 1, 2026. Presidential adviser Anwar Gargash confirmed in a May 22 statement that the decision followed three years of study and reflects the UAE's strategic view that the world is approaching the autumn of the fossil fuel era, with the goal of maximizing oil revenues before the energy transition. ADNOC CEO Al Jaber described it as a sovereign decision to enable investment flexibility.

stories.headline: Modi visits UAE, MBZ and Modi witness signing of major ADNOC-India energy agreements including 30 million barrel strategic reserve deal
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Modi visited Abu Dhabi as the first stop of a five-nation tour, meeting President MBZ. In the presence of both leaders, ADNOC signed two strategic collaboration agreements with Indian partners covering expanded crude oil storage in India's strategic petroleum reserves (up to 30 million barrels), LNG supply to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, and LPG cooperation. The visit was framed as deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during a period of Iran-driven energy insecurity.

stories.headline: Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed conducts European tour covering London, Berlin, Luxembourg, and GLOBSEC Prague to build support after Barakah attack
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed undertook an extensive working visit to European capitals in the week of May 18-23, meeting counterparts in the UK (Yvette Cooper), Germany (FM Wadephul, Interior Minister Dobrindt, Vice-Chancellor Klingbeil, Chancellor Merz, Bundestag President Klöckner), Luxembourg (Grand Duke Guillaume, PM Frieden), and Czech PM Babiš at GLOBSEC Prague. All meetings included condemnation of the Barakah drone attacks and solidarity with the UAE, alongside bilateral economic and strategic cooperation discussions.

stories.headline: Mubadala-backed Acelen secures $1.5 billion to begin construction of Brazil sustainable aviation fuel biorefinery
stories.summary: Mubadala Capital's Brazilian subsidiary Acelen Renováveis announced $1.5 billion in financing — $650 million from Mubadala and $850 million from a multilateral lending consortium including BNDES, IFC, and BID Invest — to begin construction of a sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel biorefinery in Bahia, Brazil. The plant is expected to produce one billion liters annually from 2029 and is part of Mubadala's stated $12.5 billion five-biorefinery ambition for Brazil.

stories.headline: UAE-Saudi Arabia rift deepens as new Gulf alliance blocs form over divergent Iran war approaches
stories.summary: Multiple analyses described a fracture between the UAE and Saudi Arabia that developed after the UAE exited OPEC and the two countries adopted different stances toward the Iran conflict and Israel normalization. The UAE is reported to be deepening ties with Israel while Saudi Arabia is enhancing cooperation with Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan. The ten-year alliance that had included joint operations in Yemen, Libya, and Sudan is described as under significant strain.

The company also announced a strategic partnership with Americana Restaurants to open up to 200 quick-service restaurants across ADNOC service stations in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt.

stories.headline: First ADNOC LNG tanker exits Strait of Hormuz bound for India since the war began
stories.summary: An ADNOC Logistics & Services tanker, the Al Hamra, was spotted transiting the Strait of Hormuz with an LNG cargo bound for western India — the first India-bound LNG shipment through Hormuz in approximately three months since the Iran war began. ADNOC had reportedly sent two earlier shipments to Japan and another destination but had disabled AIS transponders on tankers near its Das Island facility.

stories.headline: UAE Central Bank launches anti-fraud operations centre and orders banks to strengthen authentication beyond OTPs
stories.summary: The Central Bank of the UAE issued new guidance ordering financial institutions to move beyond single-factor authentication methods such as one-time passwords, creating a central Anti-Fraud Operations Centre. The CBUAE also issued guidance on responsible AI use in financial services and set a June 30, 2026 compliance deadline for digital brand protection requirements under an existing 2025 notice.
